State-level obstruction of private solar infrastructure is going to be a big problem going forward. I work for a leading solar manufacturer that had acquired several residential scale manufacturers (including one company that was working on solar shingles), but we're shuttering most of our residential scale work to focus solely on utility scale. Local level obstruction makes it unprofitable if not downright impossible to provide for the residential market. Once you consider the economic incentive of utility scale installations (the cost per watt decreases as installed wattage increases) there becomes a substantial market pressure for manufacturers to cater to utility-scale clients. These companies are sometimes governments or major tech companies, but often fossil fuel companies.

Under the current laws, fossil fuel companies will use their substantial on-hand funds to buy and own most of the solar generation potential. This will be a product of the pull of their purchasing power and the push away from residential because of their lobbying. The result is cheaper energy production for them at less benefit to the consumer. Yay, capitalism.
